The port states the URL and the status itself. Python's message is httpx's, which carries the reason phrase, an MDN link and the httpx version that phrased it; pinning the corpus to that text would redden this case on an httpx upgrade. The exception *name*, the failure and the records kept are identical. Recorded in the plan's §9.

Python names the httpx *subclass* the failure was — ConnectError for a refused connection, ReadTimeout for a server that accepts and never answers, ReadError for a reset (measured 2026-09-27) — and the port has one FetchError::Transport for all of them, because http.rs sees only what ureq reports. It names the *base* class, the only one that is true whichever happened, which fulltext/service.rs has always said (#361). The failure, the records kept and the URL asked for are identical; the message is the scripted transport's on both sides.
